messages:
sophia: FYI — after last night's runtime rollout that made flash_v2 the default for prefill, we're seeing p99 prefill latency spikes on long-context models (8k+). Canary showed a noticeable bump and prod followed.

rahul: saw the alert. p99 for prefill went from ~45ms -> ~120ms on the 8k chat profile. Decode path looks fine. Suspect kernel choice + batching heuristics for prefill.

jen: any KV cache anomalies? prefill shouldn't touch decode kvcache but maybe runtime routing chose a paged/fused variant that's bad at long seqs.

mateo: I pulled traces from the canary VM. Attaching short dump:

```
nsys summary:
model: chat-8k
batch dist: [1,1,2,1,3,1] (continuous batching churn)
kernel timings (per-request):
  flash_v2_prefill_kernel  88.2ms (p99)
  paged_attention_variant   9.6ms (p50)
  fused_attention_basic    12.1ms (p50)
GPU SM% = 42%, occupancy low on small sub-batches
DRAM transfers spike at prefill start (kvpage zero-copy copies)
```

rahul: that aligns with what I saw. The selector seems to be preferring flash_v2 for prefill even when the runtime microbatcher creates many tiny prefill groups due to continuous batching. Flash_v2 has fixed overheads that don't amortize on many tiny groups.

sophia: interesting — so decode routes to a small-batch-optimized path but prefill ends up using the heavy flash kernel. Could be a scoring bug in kernel_selector (weighting favors latency at large sequence length but ignores batch count).

jen: I ran a small repro on my dev GPU: toggling the kernel_selector heuristic 'use_prefill_overhead' to false drops p99 from 115ms -> 36ms for prefill on the same 8k profile. Throughput unchanged. Quick diff I used: `kernel_selector.score = base_score - overhead_penalty * microbatch_count` (I inverted the sign).

mateo: also noted KV page behavior: when microbatch_count > 4 we get repeated KV page pin/unpin which increases host<->device syncs. That interacts badly with flash_v2 because flash_v2 doesn't overlap copies as well.

benchmark-bot: perf-run #2040001 finished. summary: prefill_p99 (baseline) 45ms -> (canary) 118ms; decode_p99 stable at 28ms. regression assigned to eng-runtime.

rahul: plan: 1) revert the flash_v2 default for prefill on canary ASAP, 2) add microbatch_count into kernel scoring, 3) add a unit test for small microbatch traces to prevent future regresses.

sophia: +1. Can we do a quick canary flip first to mitigate user impact?

jen: I'll push a hotfix to flip the default to 'prefer_paged_for_prefill=true' in the rollout config and trigger a staged canary. Deploy-bot should run it.

deploy-bot: starting canary rollout: config change prefer_paged_for_prefill=true -> targets: canary pool (5% traffic)

mateo: after canary flip, metrics: prefill_p99 dropped to 48ms on canary within 10m. No change on decode. Looks good so far.

rahul: re: long-term fix — kernel_selector needs a new cost model: include microbatch_count and expected kvpage churn. I sketched a cost function: `cost = weight_time * est_lat + weight_overhead * microbatch_count * overhead_penalty + weight_copy * est_kvcopy`. We should train weights from the bench harness.

jen: I'll open a PR with the microbatch_count change + test harness using the 8k chat trace and tiny continuous batches. Assign to @rahul for review.

mateo: also filing a follow-up to improve KV page overlap for flash_v2 so that even when chosen it can overlap host copies. Might reduce worst-case overheads.

benchmark-bot: test-run queued: `eng-runtime/kernel-selector/microbatch-test` -> expected p99 < 60ms for prefill on 8k trace.

rahul: TL;DR — regression caused by heuristic that favored flash_v2 for prefill without accounting for continuous small microbatches and KV page churn. Quick mitigation = revert to paged/fused prefill on canary. Medium fix = cost model + tests. Long fix = improve flash_v2 copy overlap.

sophia: thanks all. Please post PR links and the canary result summary here when ready. I'll notify the SRE on-call if we need a broader rollback. :thumbsup:

jen: PR: https://git.redwood/s/eng-runtime/PR/4521 (microbatch scoring + tests)

mateo: canary closed at 60m, staged rollout to 20% after validation. prefill_p99 stable at ~50ms. Moving to triage->in-progress for the cost-model work.

sophia: great. leaving this thread open for any follow-ups. If anyone sees residual latency from older traces ping here.
